title: 185 Effects of diquat injection on intestinal morphology, integrity, and immunity in growing pigs
content:
Abstract
Oxidative stress (OS) is the outcome of the overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), capable of compromising the structure and physiology of the intestine in pigs. Our previous study demonstrated that diquat-induced OS reduced pigs’ growth performance and antioxidative status. Here, this study was further conducted to investigate the impact of diquat-induced OS on the small intestinal morphology, integrity, and immunity in growing pigs. Twenty individually penned barrows (average body weight, BW, of 21.5 ± 2.50 kg) were randomly allotted to two dietary treatment groups fed a corn-and-soybean-meal-based diet that met or slightly exceeded the NRC (2012) recommended requirements of nutrients and energy (SID lysine = 1.00%; SID Met+Cys = 0.62%; net energy = 2475 kcal/kg). After 3 weeks of feeding (Phase 1), while Group-1 pigs were intraperitoneally injected with 10 mL saline, Group-2 pigs were injected with 10 mg/kg BW diquat in 10 mL saline. After the injection, pigs were continually fed for 1 more week (Phase 2). At the end of Phase 2, pigs were euthanized after 12-h fasting. Ileal tissue samples were harvested and subjected to a histomorphometric analysis for the following parameters: goblet cell (GC) counts, villus height (VH), crypt depth (CD), villus width (VW), and VH:CD ratio. Furthermore, the mRNA expression levels of integrity-associated markers (Muc-1, Muc-2, and Muc-4), tight junction proteins (ZO-1, ZO-3, and CLDN-1), and proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-18, and TNF-α) were assessed quantitatively. The data was statistically analyzed using Student’s t-test. The results show that Group 2 had lower ileal mRNA levels of ZO-3 and Muc-4 (P < 0.05), and of ZO-1 at a tendency level (P = 0.07) than that in Group 1. In conclusion, this study suggested that the diquat-induced OS did not affect the expression of the small intestinal morphology and selected proinflammatory cytokine genes but impaired the small intestinal integrity in the growing pigs.
